We have reviewed the statement and offer these comments: This proposed ·legislation is much needed to insure continuing and long-term quality of our environment. This effort is commendable. In the best interest of those species whose longevity this bill is designed to foster, we recommend that the bill be amended to give sole jurisdiction over endangered species and measures to protect them to the Secretary of Interior. As pointed out in the statement and by the Florida Audubon Society; Archbold Expeditions; and Mr. A. R. Marshall, basic philosophical conflicts exist between the concepts of commercial exploitation and preservation of species. We do not believe that the Department of Commerce, being charged with the major role of sustaining maximum production of marine fishery resources, could also give maximum consideration to endangered or near endangered species; neither could the Department of Commerce, if it were charged with responsibility over endangered or near endangered species as a major role, be expected to give maximum consideration to the commercial production of marine resources. Nor do we believe that the Secretary of Commerce should be required to decide which of the two programs must suffer most.
Please append a copy of this letter, with attachments, to the final environmental impact statement submitted to the Gouncil on Environmental Quality. This will assure the Council of our compliance with guidelines implementing the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (FL 91-190).
We request that the Secretary of Interior forward us one copy of the final environmental statement submitted to the Council on environmental Quality and, in the letter of transmittal, refer to the SPDC number assigned this statement.
Sincerely,
HOMER E. STILL. JR.
